item.title: Structured Arithmetic
item.description:
DataCanon defines structured data and its identity; it does not define mathematical operations on that data. Working with structured numbers, however, naturally creates a need to calculate with them.

The Python implementation therefore includes classes for structured arithmetic. Similar in spirit to Python’s Fraction, these classes let you work with powers, sums, products, quotients, and complex numbers while retaining exact numerical structure.

These classes are a companion facility, currently distributed with DataCanon for convenience. They can be used independently of DCIs, parsing, and persistence. Their arithmetic and simplification rules belong to the language implementation, not to the DataCanon specification.

item.title: Numerical Data
item.description:
This guide explains the structure and identity of numerical DataCanon Instances. For arithmetic with Python objects, start with the Structured Arithmetic guide. Those classes can be used independently of Shorthand and persistence.

Start with a structured number

from data_canon import parse_shorthand, render_shorthand

instance = parse_shorthand("sqrt(3)")
print(instance)

The result is a Power DCI with an Integer base of 3 and direct integer exponent fields 1 and 2. sqrt(3) and power(3, 1, 2) represent equal DCIs.

A Power may have a Numerical DCI as its base: Integer, Float, Fraction, Sum, Product, Power, or Quotient. Its exponent numerator and denominator must be positive mathematical integers. They are retained independently in DCI identity.

item.title: Collections
item.description:
Most collection data already has useful Python counterparts: Lists, Tuples, Sets, and dictionaries. DataCanon also supplies Multiset and UnorderedDict for collection distinctions that need an additional Python type.

These objects follow Python’s collection behavior and equality rules. They are separate from the DCI classes that define portable DataCanon identity. The examples start with ordinary Python operations, then introduce conversion.

item.title: Shorthand Preprocessing
item.description:
Overview

Shorthand preprocessing provides three conveniences for entering scientific data by hand: compact List notation, named textual substitutions, and scalar mathematical evaluation with eval(...).

Preprocessing transforms text into strict Shorthand. Parsing that text then constructs a DataCanon Instance. This guide introduces each feature separately before showing how they work together.

Start with one compact List

Ordinary Shorthand Lists use brackets and commas:

[1, 2, 3]

item.title: Command-Line Interface
item.description:
The dc command loads a DataCanon file and displays, converts, or searches its DCI. It works with Shorthand (.dcs), canonical binary bytes (.dcb), and DataCanon HDF5 files (.h5 or .hdf5).

Put the input filename first. With no action option, dc prints Shorthand:

dc structure.dcb
